 Live .  23,209 viewing 23209 viewing Live page Updated 1 minute ago Sao Paulo qualifying fight for pole at wet Interlagos
 Live Reporting (active) 
 Leaderboard 
 Summary
 Sao Paulo Grand Prix qualifying
 Out in Q2: Hamilton, Piastri, Camara, Lindblad, Sainz, Verstappen
 Out in Q1: Colapinto, Gasly, Stroll, Bottas, Perez, Bortoleto
 Heavy rain started just before session began, leading to red flag and delay of more than 80 minutes
 Hamilton and Verstappen to start from back of grid 
 Interlagos to stay on F1 calendar until 2035
 Select 'listen live' for BBC Radio 5 Sports Extra commentary (UK only)
 Close form Send us your F1 views
 Get involved Live Reporting
 Lorraine McKenna and Tasnim Chowdhury
 Russell on provisional pole published at 20:19 GMT 20:19 GMT 
 Lando Norris goes on to provisional pole position but George Russell crosses the line to leapfrog the McLaren and pushes him down into second. 
 Liam Lawson is third on the grid as it stands, with world champion Kimi Antonelli in fourth. 
 Fernando Alonso goes again but he stays P8. 
 34 8 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 Post published at 20:18 GMT 20:18 GMT 
 So who is going to get a banker lap in and possibly sneak a surprise pole position before the rain arrives? Fernando Alonso is out on track, his last pole being way back in 2012 when he was still at Ferrari. 
 The Spaniard clocks a 1:30.311, which isn't good enough for the top, unfortunately. 
 24 22 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 Post published at 20:16 GMT 20:16 GMT 
 Sam Bird 
Former Formula E driver on 5 Sports Extra 
 At the moment I would say George Russell is my favourite [for pole position]. But Liam Lawson is looking strong, Fernando Alonso is looking strong. Honestly you could pick five or six people out there that could get pole position.
 67 13 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 Go! Go! Go! published at 20:15 GMT 20:15 GMT 
 Here we go then. 
 Bono is back on the radio to world champion Kimi Antonelli to say the rain is going to be intense. 
 Image source, Reuters 
 49 17 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 Post published at 20:14 GMT 20:14 GMT 
 The session is going to start shortly, but Kimi Antonelli is being told by Mercedes he may only get one lap in before it lashes down. 
 50 12 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 Post published at 20:12 GMT 20:12 GMT 
 The dark clouds are gathering again at Interlagos, and this could be a lot of rain that's about to be dumped on the track. 
 Q3 is delayed anyway so that the marshals can repair the barriers following Rafa Camara's crash at Turn 12, but cars are starting to line up in the pit lane, again on intermediate tyres. 
 50 10 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 Post published at 20:10 GMT 20:10 GMT 
 Harry Benjamin 
BBC F1 Commentator 
 Alex Albon Q3, his first Q3 in an incredibly long time. It has been 30 races since Alex Albon has started inside the top 10. That is what these mixed conditions can do.
 102 8 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 Post published at 20:09 GMT 20:09 GMT 
 That's not how Rafael Camara would've wanted his first qualifying to end on home soil, but the main thing is the Brazilian is out of the car safely after going straight into the barriers. 
 His off means there are some surprise names in the pole fight tonight. Alex Albon hasn't graced Q3 in ages, but the Williams man is up there after putting his car P7 in Q2. 
 Fernando Alonso has also made it through, which will bring a smile to the Aston Martin garage. 
 89 6 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 Out in Q2 published at 20:06 GMT 20:06 GMT 
 11. Lewis Hamilton (Ferrari) 
 12. Oscar Piastri (McLaren) 
 13. Rafael Camara (Haas) 
 14. Arvid Lindblad (Racing Bulls) 
 15. Carlos Sainz (Williams) 
 16. Max Verstappen (Red Bull) 
 75 46 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 Team radio - Camara to Haas published at 20:06 GMT 20:06 GMT 
 "I am sorry for that"
 52 16 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 Camara goes off published at 20:05 GMT 20:05 GMT 
 Rafael Camara has gone into the barriers at the end of this Q2 session. The Brazilian has said on the radio he is OK, and the yellow flag have now turned to red. 
 24 99 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 Post published at 20:03 GMT 20:03 GMT 
 Liam Lawson, who still doesn't know whether he'll be driving for Racing Bulls, puts his car quickest overall with a 1:27.049 on the intermediates. 
 But it's George Russell who is showing pace at Interlagos. The Mercedes man, who has a five-place grid penalty, goes above Lawson with a 1:26. 745. 
 78 14 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 Bearman goes quickest on inters published at 20:01 GMT 20:01 GMT 
 Fernando Alonso's effort on the intermediates puts him third on the timesheets, but it's Haas' Oliver Bearman who can climb the highest on the same compound with a 1:29.130. 
 91 7 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 Elimination zone published at 20:00 GMT 20:00 GMT 
 11. Rafa Camara 
 12. Arvid Lindblad 
 13. Carlos Sainz 
 14. Oliver Bearman 
 15. Alex Albon 
 16. Max Verstappen (no time) 
 56 11 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 Post published at 20:00 GMT 20:00 GMT 
 Andrew Benson 
BBC F1 correspondent 
 Alonso is on intermediates, he is the first one to try them, along with Ollie Bearman in the Haas, he has come out in them as well.
 41 4 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 Post published at 19:59 GMT 19:59 GMT 
 Red Bull think it's time for the intermediate tyres, so Isack Hadjar is heading in for the green compound. 
 Fernando Alonso has beaten the Frenchman to it, however, and the two-time world champion rejoins the track while 10th on the timesheets. 
 And off Alonso goes to start a flying lap. 
 66 6 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 Post published at 19:58 GMT 19:58 GMT 
 Arvid Lindblad is on the radio and doesn't sound happy. The British rookie is told by his Racing Bulls engineer to stop the car in a safe place. 
 19 52 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 Post published at 19:57 GMT 19:57 GMT 
 Lewis Hamilton is joining Max Verstappen at the back of the grid in Sao Paulo but on his first timed lap on the wets in Q2, the seven-time world champion goes second on the timing tower. 
 That's fourth now, though, as the Mercedes of George Russell and Kimi Antonelli find more pace to leapfrog both the Ferraris. 
 53 30 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 Post published at 19:56 GMT 19:56 GMT 
 Sam Bird 
Former Formula E driver on 5 Sports Extra 
 So we just heard Lewis Hamilton trundling out of the pitlane, making his way through the pitlane exit and that translates to the exit at Turn Three. It sounded like he had the clutch engaged and he was partial or full throttle, while going very slowly. Why would he be on full throttle, with the clutch engaged? And then he's come off the throttle and disengaged the clutch? Very strange.
 36 33 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 Post published at 19:54 GMT 19:54 GMT 
 George Russell gives up an opening time in the 1:30s but Mercedes team-mate Kimi Antonelli and McLaren's Lando Norris are up on the Briton and go quicker. 
 Charles Leclerc has a 10-place grid drop this weekend, but that doesn't stop the Monegasque driver beating his competitors to go top with a 1:29.795.
